blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established under the National Green Tribunal Act 2010 for effective and expeditious disposal of environmental protection cases.
The Tribunal is not bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but is guided by the principles of natural justice.
NGT possesses civil court powers to grant relief, compensation to victims of pollution, and restitution of damaged property or environment.
The tribunal handles civil cases arising out of seven specific environmental laws, excluding the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 and Forest Rights Act, 2006.
Appeals against decisions or orders of the NGT can be made directly to the Supreme Court of India within 90 days.

items: NGT explicitly lacks jurisdiction over the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006.
An appeal against any award, decision, or order of NGT lies directly to the Supreme Court within 90 days.
NGT mandates case disposal strictly within 6 months from the date of filing of application or appeal.
